ELLIPTIC LAB / FIELD GUIDE

From mesh to meaning.

Each square is split into two P1 triangles. The default diagonal runs from bottom left to top right, with slope +1. Dirichlet boundary values are eliminated before solving the interior system Ab = f.

01 · Start with Poisson

The default solves −Δu = 2π² sin(πx) sin(πy), with zero boundary values. Its exact solution is sin(πx) sin(πy). Try n = 4, then 16, then 32. Watch the cross-section and L² error.

02 · A sharp layer in pure Poisson

The sharp Poisson preset has an exact layer of width 0.025 near x = 1. A coarse mesh cannot resolve it. Refine the mesh to improve accuracy. Adding isotropic diffusion smooths and lowers the solution, but does not recover the missing layer.

03 · Make oscillations visible

  1. Choose Transport layer: n = 16, ε = 0.005, β = (1, 0), source = 1, δ = 0.
  2. Look near x = 1 in the cross-section: the original Galerkin solution oscillates around the exact profile. The coordinate mesh Péclet number is 6.25.
  3. Click Apply mesh-based value, which sets δ = max(0, |β|/(2n) − ε) = 0.02625.
  4. Select With diffusion or Δ Change. Compare the orange, teal, and dashed reference curves. The added diffusion reduces the oscillations and spreads the layer.
  5. Increase δ to 0.1 to see excessive smoothing. Then try n = 32 and apply the mesh-based value again.

The oscillation demo deliberately adds convection to Poisson. Classical transport instability is not a generic property of pure Poisson on this mesh. Artificial diffusion changes the equation; visual smoothness alone is not evidence of accuracy.

04 · Follow a moving front

Choose Moving front and press Play. Pure convection transports a steep smooth pulse at β = (0.55, 0), with physical ε = 0. The baseline uses consistent mass; the comparison starts with lumped mass. With δ = 0, lumping alone does not remove transport oscillations. Add mesh-based diffusion to see the front smear. Both curves use the selected time integrator; backward Euler adds more temporal damping than Crank–Nicolson.

05 · See what mass lumping helps

Choose Diffusing pulse, keeping backward Euler and δ = 0. Step forward once or scrub to t ≈ 0.005. The consistent mass solution develops negative values around the narrow pulse, while the row-sum lumped comparison remains nonnegative on this mesh. Inspect M and Mᴸ in the matrix selector and watch the negative-node counter. Positivity does not imply smaller error: this deliberately narrow initial pulse is under-resolved.

06 · Moving and spreading

Moving + diffusing solves uₜ − εΔu + β·∇u = 0. Play or scrub the trajectory; change ε, δ, Δt, mass matrix, or time integrator to compare physical spreading, artificial diffusion, and temporal damping. Every parameter change rebuilds the trajectory from the initial field and pauses playback. A shortened final step lands exactly at T.

Mass lumping replaces M by the diagonal of its full row sums before eliminating boundary nodes. It changes the time derivative, whereas δK changes spatial diffusion. Neither lumping nor Crank–Nicolson is a universal cure for convection oscillations. The baseline and comparison always share the same time integrator.

For time-dependent modes, source and boundary expressions accept t, vx, and vy. Exact Gaussian/transport traces are prescribed on all four edges in the examples. Boundary data take precedence over the initial field at boundary nodes. The consistent-mass update includes the changing-boundary term −Mᵢᵦ(gⁿ⁺¹−gⁿ); lumped mass has no off-diagonal boundary block. The integral ∫uₕ can change through these prescribed boundaries and through sources.

07 · Add reaction

The full equation is uₜ − εΔu + β·∇u + cu = f, with A = εK + C + cM. Positive c causes decay; negative c causes growth. Try Pure decay at c = 2: at t = 0.8 the exact peak is exp(−1.6) ≈ 0.202 times its initial value, with no physical spreading. Set c = 0 or −1 to compare preservation or growth. The other reaction presets isolate spreading, motion, or both. Source and boundary expressions accept c; the Gaussian boundary traces automatically include exp(−c*t).

Mass lumping here applies only to the time derivative. The reaction matrix cM remains consistent, so lumping does not guarantee positivity for stiff reaction. Crank–Nicolson can alternate in sign for stiff decay; reduce Δt and compare backward Euler. Adding diffusion smears layers and cannot correct an unresolved reaction time scale. The steady ADR preset uses a manufactured sine reference.

08 · Layers and SUPG

Try Steady outflow layer, Moving interior layer, and Developing boundary layer. Each starts with SUPG strength 1 and consistent time mass. The original curve remains unstabilized. Compare Comparison and Exact reference, then switch the comparison method to Isotropic artificial diffusion and apply the mesh-based value. Switching methods preserves the selected time.

SUPG tests the element equation residual along the flow: τ(β·∇v)(uₜ − εΔu + β·∇u + cu − f). For P1 triangles, the element Laplacian vanishes. The spatial correction S, time correction H, source correction, and boundary lifts are all included. Isotropic diffusion spreads in every direction; SUPG's leading diffusion acts along β, with no added crosswind diffusion.

The steady example has a thin layer at x = 1. The moving example transports a steep pulse; at t = 0.8 SUPG reduces its oscillations but still leaves undershoot. The developing example uses u = (1−exp(−t))q(x) with a manufactured source and exact traces: its outflow layer grows from zero. This is a controlled accuracy example, not an unforced startup.

SUPG is not a positivity guarantee and does not resolve a layer narrower than the mesh. Compare L² error, extrema, and the cross-section, then refine n. No flow means no SUPG: for a pure reaction–diffusion layer, refine the mesh instead. Algebraic A/f edits are combined with SUPG assembled from the physical PDE, so those experiments are not residual-consistent with the edited system.

Edit a real matrix entry

Use n = 4 for a 9 × 9 interior system. In Matrix A, double A[4,4] from 4 to 8: the center drops. In Load f, increase f[4]: the center rises. Matrix edits apply to A before δK. With nonzero boundary data, the stabilized load also includes the extra boundary contribution −δKᵢᵦg.

Conventions & limits

Global node IDs run left to right, bottom to top. Free DOFs follow that order with boundary nodes removed. Changes to the mesh clear indexed edits; PDE changes retain them. Presets and Reset clear all edits. Boundary corners average conflicting edge values; a node override takes precedence.

The solver uses double precision with partial pivoting in a Web Worker. L² error is a degree-five quadrature estimate, not a certified bound. The mesh-based diffusion value is a useful starting point, not a guarantee for arbitrary transport directions or edited matrices. The exact reference is hidden after changes that invalidate it.
